note: Frozen check list for explain evals 1-10. Written before any run of these evals and not to be edited to fit an output. Its author had read no output of the skill: the trigger transcripts of 2026-11-21 hold no explanation, and of SKILL.md only the description had been read, in the trigger results. Each assertion in evals.json is decomposed into atomic yes/no checks. kind=file and kind=absence are decided by a script from the bytes on disk after the run; where the eval has no fixture the only file is the reply, and the checks on emoji, on '5432', on headings and on list items are decided on it. kind=reply, kind=invention and kind=negative are decided by an LLM judge. A met kind=reply check quotes the words that satisfy it. kind=invention and kind=negative are negatives: when met there is nothing to quote and the evidence is the search; when unmet the offending words are quoted. In evals 7, 8 and 9 the reply holds a text meant for someone else next to the reply's own remarks to the user; a check that says 'the text', 'the email' or 'the revised reply' is about that text only. Counts (sentences, lines, words) are judged, not scripted, because a script cannot tell that text from the remarks; a judge counts badly near a limit, so a borderline count resolves to not met like any other borderline case. More text never raises a verdict. No anchor cases: the two earlier lists got theirs by dated amendment after judges split.

1.check: The reply is written in Portuguese (quote its first sentence)
The reply asks the user no question before the explanation starts
Within its first two sentences the reply states what a mutex is: something that lets only one goroutine or thread at a time run a piece of code or touch a value (quote the sentence)

The reply contains a concrete case with specific values or a specific sequence of events (for example two goroutines incrementing the same counter and one update being lost), not only a general statement (quote it)
The reply does not open by praising the question ('Ótima pergunta', 'Claro!')
The reply does not open by restating the question ('Você quer saber o que é um mutex')
The reply does not explain what a variable or a function is

No concurrency term the user did not use (race condition or condição de corrida, critical section or seção crítica, goroutine scheduling) appears without being defined or replaced where it first appears. A reply that uses none of them passes
No analogy in the reply is left without saying what corresponds to what. A reply with no analogy passes
No analogy in the reply is left without saying where it stops working. A reply with no analogy passes

The reply does not end with a generic offer of more help ('Se tiver mais dúvidas, é só perguntar', 'Quer que eu explique mais?'). A question that checks the reader's understanding, or an offer of one specific thing, is not a generic offer
